The table contains no row for a damage-taken amplifier; it does establish that mitigation is linear in raw damage ("mitigation commutes with expectation (linear in raw)"), so a flat percentage 'increased damage taken' rides as a scalar multiplier on the damage instance and may be applied either pre- or post-mitigation with the same result.

independent_computation.step_1_effect_identification: Bloodsong (id 3877) is a Legendary support item whose UNIQUE passive Spellblade, on the empowered basic attack against a champion, inflicts 'Expose Weakness' for 4 s. Expose Weakness is a debuff on the TARGET that increases the damage it takes from ALL sources — i.e. it is a team-wide amplifier available to every participant hitting that target, which is exactly what a per-event 'support_damage_multiplier' on the attacker's combat event models.
independent_computation.step_2_template_resolution: The amp magnitude in the cached wikitext is {{rd|8%|5%}}. {{rd|A|B}} is the League Wiki's ranged-difference template: A applies when the ITEM HOLDER is melee, B when the holder is ranged. Calibrated against three independently-known items (Death's Dance 30/10, Hydra cleave 40%/20% AD, Serpent's Fang 50/35) and internally cross-checked with Yun Tal Wildarrows, where 63 × 0.4% = 25.2% and 125 × 0.2% = 25.0% both land on the item's stated 25% crit cap — only the melee-first reading makes both branches self-consistent.
independent_computation.step_3_arithmetic: Expose Weakness = +8% damage taken (melee holder). A '+X% increased damage taken' debuff is a scalar multiplier on the damage instance: multiplier = 1 + X = 1 + 0.08 = 1.08. Ranged-holder branch would be 1 + 0.05 = 1.05. With no other 'increased damage taken' source present in this leaf's receipt, no additive stacking of amp terms applies, so the multiplier is exactly the single term.
independent_computation.step_4_old_value: The old value <absent> is equivalent to no amplifier (multiplier 1.0). Under either branch of {{rd|8%|5%}} the wiki mandates a non-unity amplifier on any damage event landing inside the 4 s Expose Weakness window after a Bloodsong Spellblade proc on a champion, so 'absent' cannot be the correct modelling of an event that the scenario's own receipt attributes to 'Bloodsong — Expose Weakness'. old_value_correct is ruled out.
independent_computation.result: 1.08 for a melee Bloodsong holder; 1.05 for a ranged Bloodsong holder. The published new value 1.08 is the exact, correctly-derived melee branch.

residual_uncertainty.statement: The one input I could not obtain inside the permitted evidence tree is the ATTACK TYPE of the Bloodsong-holding ally in this scenario's roster. The scenario definition 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' lives outside data/ and docs/math-foundations.md (it is not in data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json, data/worklists/, or anywhere else in the export), and src/, tests/ and scripts/ are out of bounds for this runbook.
residual_uncertainty.decision_rule_for_the_parent: If the Bloodsong holder in the roster has attackType MELEE → 1.08 is exactly right (verdict stands). If the holder has attackType RANGED → the correct value is 1.05 and the leaf is wrong (verdict would become both_wrong, since <absent> is wrong too).
residual_uncertainty.attack_type_lookup_is_in_the_cache: data/champions.json carries an explicit attackType per champion, so the check is mechanical. Spot values gathered for the common support pool: Leona MELEE (125), Pyke MELEE (150), Nautilus MELEE (175); Thresh RANGED (450 — a frequent trap, Thresh is ranged for item melee/ranged splits), Senna RANGED (600), Lulu RANGED (550), Janna RANGED (550).
residual_uncertainty.why_the_verdict_is_still_new_value_corre: 1.08 is not an arbitrary number — it reproduces the melee branch of the cached wiki text to the digit, including the correct 1+X multiplier form and the correct 'all sources' team-wide semantics that justify a support_damage_multiplier field at all. A hardcoded-8%-ignoring-the-split defect is possible but is not evidenced by anything in the permitted tree, whereas the value's exact agreement with a real branch of the source formula is.

notes: Bloodsong's Expose Weakness also carries a 1.5 s internal cooldown starting after the empowered attack and a 4 s debuff duration; those govern WHICH events carry the multiplier, not its magnitude, and were not evaluable from data/ alone.

Aside (off-task, from data/champions.json Gangplank notes): the cache records 'Bloodsong: Dealing damage with kegs to champions won't apply Expose Weakness to them' — a real exclusion if a Gangplank scenario ever routes Spellblade through Powder Kegs.
